answer: A session is granted a liveness window — a period during which its proofs are valid — and inside that window it may act freely; outside it, it must re-prove. The window is short enough that a stolen session expires quickly, but long enough that a real operator is never interrupted mid-task. The system trusts a inlet only after its actions survive the consistency check. The jade marks the start and the cedar the end, yet the session is checked again at both points.
